item.title: TIPNG report warns PNG’s civic freedoms under pressure
item.description: In a report, Transparency International Papua New Guinea (TIPNG) raises concern over the increasing pressure on civic freedoms in PNG. TIPNG’s Enabling Environment Baseline Snapshot 2025, shows trends seen over the past six months. Issues include inappropriate laws, weak enforcement of constitutional protections, and restrictions to civic and digital spaces. item.title: Petrol price drops by 12t, as diesel rises in Feb
item.description: The Independent Consumer and Competition Commission (‘ICCC’) announced today the new retail fuel prices for this month, which will take effect (Today) Sunday, 8th February 2026. For this month, the Indicative Retail Prices (‘IRP’) for petrol and kerosene will decrease on average while for diesel will increase, throughout the nation. item.title: K120 million power projects promise end to Lae blackouts
item.description: Lae city’s longstanding power problem will be over with the launching and commissioning of two new electricity generation projects on Friday. The National Government has injected close to K120 million into Lae’s power generation with the launch of the Yalu Solar Farm Project and the commissioning of eight new generators at East Taraka Sub Station, a move expected to fix the long-standing electricity problem and restore business confidence in Lae city. item.title: PM Marape hails record coffee production as proof PNG can prosper through agriculture
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has welcomed the announcement by Minister for Coffee William Bando that Papua New Guinea exported more than 1.5 million Bags of Coffee in 2025, describing the achievement as a clear signal that the nation’s Agriculture Sector is rebounding strongly and that PNG can grow wealth directly from the land owned by its people.
